targets.approach: Rock Springs Buttress is reached from the Jackson Hole ski area: park in the upper lot behind the lodge, hike the paved road toward the Union Pass lift, take the small trail that leaves to the left where the road ends, then turn left onto the service road, which steepens into a trail up to the buttress. From the top of the tram a cairned climbers' trail descends from the ridge into the base area instead. The route is on the Central Sector, the part of the cliff with the tallest multi-pitch lines, between Crucify the Dread on its left and Red, Green and Gold on its right. A large loose gully separates this sector from the smaller West Sector.
targets.name: Big Wall(y) Gets The Chop

targets.approach: Rock Springs Buttress is reached from the Jackson Hole ski area: park in the upper lot behind the lodge, hike the paved road toward the Union Pass lift, take the small trail that leaves to the left where the road ends, then turn left onto the service road, which steepens into a trail up to the buttress. From the top of the tram a cairned climbers' trail descends from the ridge into the base area instead. The line is a variation on the top of the route XM on the Central Sector: it follows XM to the last bolt before the final roof, then breaks left to a thin crack, pulls the roof beside the arete, and follows the arete to the anchors.
targets.name: Whipper Direct

targets.approach: Start at the Leigh Lake parking area and walk the trail northward, then pick up the signs pointing to the Leigh Lake portage. Boulder Island sits just offshore, a short swim from the lake edge, or a paddle across from the same trailhead. The route is on the west side of the main boulder, following the clear finger crack immediately to the right of the black dike.
targets.name: Bohemianism Original Route

targets.approach: The route is in Boy Scout Cirque in Teton Canyon, at the far right side of the cirque, beyond the Boy Scout couloir and the big roof dihedrals. It follows a diagonal crack to a left-facing dihedral.
targets.descent_text: Descend by rappel from the sling anchors at the top of the climb.
targets.name: Where's Bernie?

targets.approach: Rock Springs Buttress is reached from the Jackson Hole ski area: park in the upper lot behind the lodge, hike the paved road toward the Union Pass lift, take the small trail that leaves to the left where the road ends, then turn left onto the service road, which steepens into a trail up to the buttress. From the top of the tram a cairned climbers' trail descends from the ridge into the base area instead. The East Sector is the first part of the cliff reached from below: from the talus under the Central Sector, contour right (east), or take the faint trail that branches right once inside Rock Springs Canyon. From the tram top, pass the West Sector and keep along the base of the Central Sector beyond the big slab. This line is the upper part of For Pete's Sake, normally reached by climbing the lower pitches of Swordfish Lipstick.
targets.name: For Pete’s Sake

targets.approach: Cascade Canyon is reached by the short boat ride across Jenny Lake or on foot around the lake, then the horse trail that joins the main canyon trail. The route begins beneath the obvious Bat Attack Crack: easy slabs and a trough lead to the right side of the arching roof, where this line breaks out right around the roof, sharing that start.
targets.descent_text: Walk the ramp that traverses left to the comfortable ledge at the top of the pitch and rappel from the fixed anchor there back to the ground.
targets.name: Hot Dogs

targets.approach: Cascade Canyon is reached by the short boat ride across Jenny Lake or on foot around the lake, then the horse trail that joins the main canyon trail. Baxter's Pinnacle is only a short walk up the trail before the turn-off. The route is a variation on the first pitch of the Baxter's Pinnacle South Ridge: it starts right below the first tree on the fourth-class approach scramble, partway up from the base, on a steep, thin orange slab just north of the standard line.
targets.name: Seizure Disorder

targets.approach: From the Death Canyon trailhead (reached by the Moose-Wilson road and a dirt road off it), hike past Phelps Lake and up Death Canyon, passing below The Snaz, Caveat Emptor and Aerial Boundaries. Once beyond the last switchbacks on the lower trail the route is easy to spot: the single full-height dihedral cutting the west side of Cathedral Rock. Follow the loose gully that runs beneath the west face; the climb starts a little higher than the lower end of the steep, fourth-class gully used to descend from The Snaz.
targets.descent_text: Descend by the Snaz walk-off: the descent chimneys and gully to the south of the buttress.
targets.name: The Widowmaker

targets.approach: The Cirque of the Moon sits on the south side of the Popo Agie's North Fork. It is entered from Dickinson Park on the Shoshone National Forest roads north of Lander, following the trail down to the river and up through forest onto the boulder floor of the cirque, or by the longer way through the Cirque of the Towers from the Big Sandy trailhead. The line is on Sumac Point's northern end, facing southwest, and lies off to the left as you climb into the cirque.
targets.name: Brokeback Mountain

targets.approach: The Cirque of the Moon sits on the south side of the Popo Agie's North Fork. It is entered from Dickinson Park on the Shoshone National Forest roads north of Lander, following the trail down to the river and up through forest onto the boulder floor of the cirque, or by the longer way through the Cirque of the Towers from the Big Sandy trailhead. The line aims at the prominent dihedral high on Sunset Buttress. The lower part of the buttress is easy, unprotectable slab and broken ground with many ways up to a grassy platform at the foot of a right-facing corner, which can also be reached by walking in from the right.
targets.name: Buffalo Nudes

targets.approach: The Cirque of the Moon sits on the south side of the Popo Agie's North Fork. It is entered from Dickinson Park on the Shoshone National Forest roads north of Lander, following the trail down to the river and up through forest onto the boulder floor of the cirque, or by the longer way through the Cirque of the Towers from the Big Sandy trailhead. The wall is among the first on your left when entering the cirque: Sumac Point's far-left wall, to the right of Bo Mambo. Walk up the ramp from camp, passing Forest Creatures, until you reach the wall's foot; the start is right of the conspicuous tree.
targets.name: Martian Moonbase

targets.approach: The Cirque of the Moon sits on the south side of the Popo Agie's North Fork. It is entered from Dickinson Park on the Shoshone National Forest roads north of Lander, following the trail down to the river and up through forest onto the boulder floor of the cirque, or by the longer way through the Cirque of the Towers from the Big Sandy trailhead. The route is just right of Martian Moonbase on the lower part of Sumac Point. Take the third-class ledge to the tree, then from the right side of that ledge climb toward the open-book feature and the large chimney above.
targets.name: Orbital Spin

targets.approach: The Cirque of the Moon sits on the south side of the Popo Agie's North Fork. It is entered from Dickinson Park on the Shoshone National Forest roads north of Lander, following the trail down to the river and up through forest onto the boulder floor of the cirque, or by the longer way through the Cirque of the Towers from the Big Sandy trailhead. The route lies on North Sumac Point's southwest side, a little right of Brokeback Mountain. Start at the base of the wall beside the boulders where the rubble pile heads up into the gully, and aim for the left base of the crack that emerges from the apex of the prominent arch.
targets.name: Reginald's Roar

targets.approach: The Cirque of the Moon sits on the south side of the Popo Agie's North Fork. It is entered from Dickinson Park on the Shoshone National Forest roads north of Lander, following the trail down to the river and up through forest onto the boulder floor of the cirque, or by the longer way through the Cirque of the Towers from the Big Sandy trailhead. The route is on the west face of Sumac Point and starts under the right-facing dihedral formed by a big block.
targets.name: Two Left Feet

targets.approach: The Cirque of the Sun is a small cirque just south of Monolith Cirque. Hike in from Dickinson Park, outside Lander, along the North Fork trail; the final climb into the cirque is brief but steep, and inside it the walls are simple to reach. The route starts just left of the start of Solar Winds.
targets.name: Ghost Hamster

targets.approach: The Cirque of the Sun is a small cirque just south of Monolith Cirque, reached by the North Fork trail that starts at Dickinson Park near Lander. The route sits on the way in to Icarus. Find a tall column standing apart from the buttress with a big boulder beside it on the right, and start in the gap between them.
targets.descent_text: Every belay carries fixed hardware for rappelling the route, as far up as the crux pitch.
targets.name: Interstellar Marmot (5.12- A0)

targets.approach: From the Lupine Meadows parking lot, follow the Lupine Meadows trail to the junction with the Surprise and Amphitheater Lakes trail, pass Surprise Lake to the camping area, and head north between the two lakes until Delta Lake comes into view. Follow the cliff band that runs east along the south side of Delta Lake. The route is on a west-facing slab where the cliff noticeably juts out, near two spruce trees with gnarled roots; the base is reached by scrambling down or rappelling in.
targets.name: Shenanagain

targets.approach: Drive Highway 16 west from Buffalo, turn right at the Hunter Creek Trailhead sign, take the left fork onto Forest Service Road 391 (rocky; high clearance is recommended) and park at the Enormodome camp, just right of the road at the edge of a large meadow. A faint path leads north from camp to a cattle trail heading northeast; leave it to skirt the boggy meadow on its north side, and a cleared path through the young forest runs straight to the south prow of the dome. The East Face is on the east flank of the fin. This route starts just left of the old buck-rail fence that meets the wall, immediately left of Task Force Master.
targets.descent_text: Lower off the clip-and-lower anchors at the top, which it shares with Task Force Master.
targets.name: On the Fence

targets.approach: Drive Highway 16 west from Buffalo, turn right at the Hunter Creek Trailhead sign, take the left fork onto Forest Service Road 391 (rocky; high clearance is recommended) and park at the Enormodome camp, just right of the road at the edge of a large meadow. A faint path leads north from camp to a cattle trail heading northeast; leave it to skirt the boggy meadow on its north side, and a cleared path through the young forest runs straight to the south prow of the dome. The East Face is on the east flank of the fin. The route shares its start with On the Fence, immediately left of where the old buck-rail fence meets the wall.
targets.descent_text: Lower off the clip-and-lower anchors at the top.
targets.name: Rockdust Torture

targets.approach: Drive Highway 16 west from Buffalo, turn right at the Hunter Creek Trailhead sign, take the left fork onto Forest Service Road 391 (rocky; high clearance is recommended) and park at the Enormodome camp, just right of the road at the edge of a large meadow. A faint path leads north from camp to a cattle trail heading northeast; leave it to skirt the boggy meadow on its north side, and a cleared path through the young forest runs straight to the south prow of the dome. The East Face is on the east flank of the fin. The route is the fifth from the left, starting immediately right of a white dike.
targets.descent_text: Lower off the clip-and-lower anchors at the top.
targets.name: Task Force Master

targets.approach: The East Fork Road area is BLM land in the East Fork drainage near Dubois. The crack line lies down the hill from Welcome to Dubois, in a canyon with rock outcrops on both sides, below a ranch gate at the top of the hill on East Fork Road. It is reached by rappelling into the canyon.
targets.name: Midnight rider.

targets.approach: The East Fork Road area is BLM land in the East Fork drainage near Dubois. Keep following East Fork Road past the Bear Creek Road turn-off to a ranch gate at the top of a hill, with a canyon below and rock outcrops on both sides. The climb is reached by building a rappel station at the top and rappelling in.
targets.name: Welcome to dubois.

targets.approach: Follow the Dry Horse Creek trail up to the saddle that divides Dry from Wet Horse Creek, then follow the ridge southwest through mountain mahogany to the base of the tower. Ledge systems on either side make it easy to traverse around the tower. The route is on the southwest side of the Eocene tower and begins in the left-hand corner, on the rock bridge's south side, where it links the Eocene with Brokeback.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the southwest face from the summit, using an intermediate anchor partway down before the last rappel to the ground.
targets.name: Eohippus

targets.approach: False Rock is a rock pillar in the Bighorn Basin. Take the two-track road to the foot of the mountain, follow the bottom of the canyon until you are close to the tower, then take the draw on the left side of the tower. The route is on the north side of the rock, beside the big crack.
targets.name: John 3:16

targets.approach: This is a small practice boulder in the Meadows camping zone of Garnet Canyon, the first thing on the left (south) as you enter the zone, on the east side near the crossing of the north fork. The west-facing slab is the practice surface.
targets.name: Friction Pitch Boulder
targets.parent: Garnet Canyon Rock Climbs-Not Disappointment Peak

targets.name: Meadows Marquee
targets.parent: Garnet Canyon Rock Climbs-Not Disappointment Peak

targets.approach: The Ice Cream Cone is a spire just east of the South Teton on the ridge that runs to Cloudveil Dome. It is reached from the west by the South Teton's east face, or from the east via Cloudveil Dome and neighbouring peaks; approaching it directly is not practical because of loose rock and rockfall. The route begins in the col where the Cone meets the South Teton's east ridge, up the evident dark chimney or wide crack that has a low chockstone close to the ground.
targets.name: West Face
targets.parent: Garnet Canyon Rock Climbs-Not Disappointment Peak

targets.approach: Index is a granite spire in the Five Fingers, on the Bighorn divide in the Cloud Peak Wilderness, south of the Thumb. Hike in from the east (through Highland Park, passing Spear Lake on the way to Loomis Lake) or from the west (starting at Lower Paintrock Lake and crossing the Cliff Lakes country). The route begins at the foot of the orange-coloured east ridge.
targets.descent_text: From the summit, downclimb north, then rappel past a large ledge into the talus-filled descent gully.
targets.name: Pika Hunter

targets.approach: The Island is a granite plug rising directly above the Cody climbers parking area. Drive west from Cody through Shoshone Canyon on Highway 14/16, pass the two short tunnels, and park at the pull-in on the highway's north side ahead of the long tunnel. The route follows the featured crack on the northwest face of the Island, reached by going over the hill on the Green Mile approach and down the trail, then turning sharply left to a belay platform beneath the scree field.
targets.name: Green Slime

targets.approach: The Island is a granite plug rising directly above the Cody climbers parking area, reached by driving west from Cody through Shoshone Canyon on Highway 14/16 and parking at the pull-in on the highway's north side ahead of the long tunnel. The route takes the Island's south arete, left of Jesus Loves You and near the parking lot, and begins on a wide hand-and-fist crack.
targets.name: South Ridge

targets.approach: Little Seneca Lake lies on the way from the Elkhart Park trailhead (Pole Creek trail) toward Island Lake and Gannett Peak. The route is on the north side of the lake, a few yards from the water. Follow the trail along the west shore round to the north side, pass the black-streaked rock on your left, leave the trail toward the shore at the first opportunity, continue past Gymnast In My Duffle Bag and around a rock outcrop. The first big crack system past the outcrop, on its east side, is the route.
targets.descent_text: Walk off easily to climber's left, or rappel from trees above the route.
targets.name: Jealous of Jentry

targets.approach: Monolith Cirque is reached along the North Fork trail that starts at Dickinson Park, or across Jack Ass Pass from Big Sandy. The A-Frame Buttress, which looks like its name, stands on climber's right at the entrance to the cirque; the route follows its obvious crack system.
targets.descent_text: Come down from the top by way of easy ledges and gullies.
targets.name: A-Frame Buttress: Standard Route

targets.approach: Monolith Cirque is reached along the North Fork trail that starts at Dickinson Park, or across Jack Ass Pass from Big Sandy. The route climbs the steep northeast face of the Monolith, the large formation on the cirque.
targets.name: Children of the Sun (Free 1988)

targets.approach: Monolith Cirque is reached along the North Fork trail that starts at Dickinson Park, or across Jack Ass Pass from Big Sandy. Walk straight from the lake to the foot of the line, which takes the prominent chimney and crack system straight up the middle of the largest formation in the cirque and leans left near the top.
targets.descent_text: The summit is a surprisingly flat plateau. Walk down gentle, non-technical ground well to the east of the formation and back into the cirque.
targets.name: Monolith, North Face, Gran Route

targets.approach: The Mouth refers to a pair of limestone massifs where Clark's Fork Canyon opens out. From Cody go north on Wyoming Highway 120 to Clark, turn west at the Edelweiss Restaurant onto Canyon Road 1AB, trend left onto the road that follows to the canyon mouth, and walk a short way from the highway across a BLM fence to the routes. This line is the lower part of the route Forever.
targets.name: Almost Forever

targets.approach: Climb to the upper ledge system of High Plains Hoedown, walk right along the ledge until you can head up the massive gully system, and hike and scramble up it by the easiest line (if it becomes fifth class you have gone wrong) to the base of the large slab that sits left of a huge corner system capped with a tree ledge.
targets.descent_text: Rappel back down the route, then scramble down and rappel High Plains Hoedown to finish.
targets.name: The East Face

targets.approach: The North Side Rock Climbs buttresses stand over the northern shore of Taminah Lake, in Avalanche Canyon. They are a short hike up from the lake, bearing left as you gain height so as to skirt the lower cliff band in between. The approach is only a little longer than the one to Irene's Arete.
targets.name: Blind Man's Bluff

targets.approach: Reach Omega Buttress from the Death Canyon trailhead: hike to the Phelps Lake overlook, descend into Death Canyon, and climb the talus and loose gully to the base of the buttress. Begin from a tree on a small grassy ledge a short way west of the standard slab start shared by all Ship's Prow routes, below the obvious crack.
targets.descent_text: For a one-pitch outing, belay from the ledge, then scramble east to a large tree that can be used for the descent.
targets.name: Pitch One 5.10 Variation (Ship's Prow)

targets.approach: The route is on the Sawtooth ridge right above Powder River Pass, the high point of Highway 16, so the walk to the base is short. It follows the steepest line up cracks and jug rails to the ridge, then continues north along the crest to the grass.
targets.descent_text: From the crest, circle east around the talus to return to the pass, or retrace the ridge.
targets.name: Powder River Let ‘er Buck

targets.approach: Ram's Head Buttress is in the northern Wind River Range, in the Green River area, beyond the second lake. The route is on the left panel of the buttress, starting at the bottom of the ridge feature to the right of that panel and following slabs, chimneys and broken ground up the ridge.
targets.descent_text: Walk off to climber's right of the buttress.
targets.name: "Ram's Head Buttress"
